added: A new figure, forward and back, names the formation dancers go forward and back in: long lines, in squares, lines of three, four, five or six, as couples, head couples, side couples, in a ring, in lines at heads or in lines at sides. It shows in the figure's line (“lines of three forward & back”, or “in a ring forward” when the dancers don't come back), and typing that line into the dance editor reads it back as the figure.
changed: Long lines is now forward and back in long lines. Your long lines figures are unchanged and still read “long lines”; changing a long lines figure's formation turns it into a forward and back, and a forward and back set to long lines is saved as long lines.
Typing just “forward and back” into the dance editor now reads it as long lines, the usual formation, instead of keeping it as text.

A dialect's own name or wording for long lines keeps applying to it, and a name you give forward and back does not rename long lines. The dialect editor, Advanced search's Has figure and the per-figure defaults in Settings still offer long lines on its own.
A program matrix column you built on long lines keeps counting long lines, and opens in the column editor as forward and back in long lines.
data_migrations: Taxonomy 39: no migration and no index rebuild; long lines figures you already have are stored, shown and searched exactly as before.
Devices still on 0.9.x show a forward and back figure by its internal name, as they do any figure added since. Long lines figures entered on this version read there exactly as before.

added: Add the `forward_and_back` move (taxonomy v39): `formation` (a `ParamKind.choice` of `forwardAndBackFormations`, default `longLines`), `goBack` and `beats`, with long lines' `goBack`-driven beats. Add `forwardAndBackFormations`.
Add `MoveAlias.listedAsMove`: such an alias is offered where moves are and aliases are not, and a dialect's name and wording for it apply to it while its target's never do. Set for `long_lines` only.

Add `Taxonomy.withoutListedAliasPins`: the params a figure stores without the value an alias listed as a move pins. The dance repository's write-time routing, the free-text read-back and `switchUserFigureUsesIn` (which also routes a use switched to long lines to `long_lines`) apply it, so a `long_lines` never stores `formation`.
Add `savedMatrixConstraint`: a matrix column or compound step on `forward_and_back` stating `formation: longLines` is saved on `long_lines` without it.
changed: `long_lines` is now an alias of `forward_and_back` pinning `formation: longLines`, with `inversePairId: forward_and_back`, so `resolvedMoveId` routes between the two on `formation`. Its canonical text (`long lines`) and display lines are unchanged; its effective params gain `formation: longLines`. Free-text entry's typed names and the figure editor's move pick start a figure under the id it is stored with, so a bare `forward_and_back` starts as `long_lines`.

Render a `forward_and_back` as `<formation> forward & back` (verbose `forward and back`), or `<formation> forward` without `goBack`; canonical text is `<formation> forward and back`. The renderer's camelCase humanizer, and the app's `humanizeToken`, break before a capital that starts a word after a one-letter word (`inARing` → `in a ring`).
Free-text entry reads a displayed forward and back back as that figure; the import grammar is unchanged.

Program matrix parameterized and compound columns whose base move is an alias match its target with the alias's pinned params added, and a column for an alias listed as a move is labelled by the dialect's name for that alias.
`figureSnippetSignature` of an alias listed as a move is its own id without its pinned params, so every `long_lines` keeps the signature `long_lines`.
`FilterCompiler` never maps an alias's id through a dialect's move names, as it already did not a move's.
